What they offer: Free and low-cost breast exams, screening and diagnostic mammograms, and Pap smears for uninsured or underinsured women.
Who qualifies: Mecklenburg County residents with income at or below 250% of the federal poverty level. Mammograms ages 40 to 64, Pap tests ages 21 to 64.
Documents to bring: Proof of income (checked at enrollment). Signs a BCCCP consent form before the visit.

What they offer: Free screening mammograms on a mobile unit, with follow-up exams and biopsies when needed. Project PINK Plus offers a free diagnostic mammogram for women with a lump or other breast concern.
Who qualifies: Women 40 and older living in Mecklenburg or Union County without insurance that covers an annual mammogram.
Volunteer tips: Contact by email: LCIOutreach@AtriumHealth.org. Ask about upcoming screening dates.

What they offer: Grant funding to help cover mammograms for uninsured patients.
Who qualifies: Uninsured Charlotte-area residents. Confirm current criteria by phone.
Volunteer tips: Spanish line: 704-384-8202. Older listing, verify first.

What they offer: Bilingual health center: primary care, chronic disease management, dental clinic, nutrition, and behavioral health (Camino Contigo: individual and group therapy, peer support).
Who qualifies: Focus on low-income, uninsured and underinsured families, especially the Latino community.
Volunteer tips: Sources say they serve people regardless of immigration status. Confirm when verifying.
Source: Camino website; Enlace Latino NC; WFAE 2025

What they offer: Food pantry for families in need.
Who qualifies: Confirm current eligibility.

What they offer: Federally qualified health center: primary care, dental and behavioral health, plus HIV/STI testing and PrEP for uninsured patients.
Who qualifies: Low-income insured and uninsured adults. Fees on a sliding scale by household income.
Address: 8401 Medical Plaza Dr, Suite 300, Charlotte, NC 28262
Source: CDC GetTested; CMS school resource page

What they offer: Family health care including primary care, behavioral health, dentistry and case management, regardless of ability to pay.
Who qualifies: Open to all. Fees based on ability to pay.

What they offer: Primary care in person and by virtual visit: physical exams and care for common conditions like diabetes, high blood pressure and high cholesterol.
Who qualifies: Uninsured or underinsured patients. Affordable visit fees.
Address: Ascend Nonprofit Solutions building, 601 E 5th St, Suite 140, Charlotte, NC 28202
Source: NSON volunteer page; NPI listing (phone, address)

What they offer: Connects patients to a network of volunteer doctors, specialists, dentists, labs and hospitals that donate care, including primary care, surgery, orthopedics and cancer care.
Who qualifies: Low-income Mecklenburg County residents with no insurance, Medicaid or Medicare.
Documents to bring: Proof of Mecklenburg County residency and income documents (eligibility screening).
Volunteer tips: Best option for specialty care: specialists, labs and imaging.

What they offer: A free personal nurse who gives support, advice and information during pregnancy and after the baby arrives.
Who qualifies: First-time mothers. Confirm other criteria.

What they offer: Community health worker program to improve health before, during and after pregnancy and reduce disparities in infant and maternal outcomes.
Who qualifies: Residents of six Mecklenburg County priority health zip codes.

What they offer: Free prescription medications mailed to the patient's home, usually a 90-day supply.
Who qualifies: Uninsured North Carolina residents under an income limit (sources list 200% to 300% of the federal poverty level).
Documents to bring: Written prescription, proof of residency, proof of income.
Address: 4428 Taggart Creek Rd, Suite 101, Charlotte, NC 28208
Source: Mecklenburg County CIT; WIZS; NC Treasurer

What they offer: Free over-the-counter medicine, vitamins, medical supplies and hygiene items.
Who qualifies: Any North Carolina resident.
Address: 4428 Taggart Creek Rd, Suite 101, Charlotte, NC 28208
Volunteer tips: Check current store hours before sending a patient.

What they offer: 24/7 line to find mental health, substance use and developmental disability services.
Who qualifies: People with Medicaid, or uninsured or underinsured, in Mecklenburg County.
Volunteer tips: Start here for uninsured patients who need therapy or psychiatry. Crisis line: 877-223-4617.

What they offer: Walk-in mental and behavioral health services for adults and children.
Who qualifies: Confirm insurance and fees by phone.
Address: 5700 Executive Center Dr, Suite 110, Charlotte, NC 28212
Hours: Mon-Thu 8 a.m. to 3 p.m., Fri 8 a.m. to 1 p.m.
Source: CMS school resource page; Mecklenburg Public Health

What they offer: Free civil legal help: housing and eviction, income and benefits, health care access, taxes, wills for seniors, and immigration through the Immigrant Justice Program.
Who qualifies: Low-income residents. Does not handle criminal charges.
Volunteer tips: Spanish line: 800-247-1931. No walk-ins for immigration.
Source: Mecklenburg County CIT; US DOJ pro bono list

What they offer: Free legal help in civil matters for low-income people.
Who qualifies: Low-income. Civil cases only.

What they offer: Referral to a private attorney when free legal aid can't take the case.
Who qualifies: Anyone. Attorney fees apply.
Volunteer tips: Use when legal aid can't help, for example criminal cases.

Organization: Nourish Up (formerly Loaves & Fishes / Friendship Trays)
What they offer: About a week of groceries from pantry sites across Charlotte.
Who qualifies: Requires a referral. The referring partner calls Nourish Up on the person's behalf.
Documents to bring: The referring partner needs each household member's name and date of birth, plus address and phone.
Who can refer: Clergy, medical providers, school counselors, human service agencies, Latin American Coalition (704-531-3848)
Volunteer tips: Ask whether NSON can become a referring partner.

What they offer: Emergency food pantry.
Who qualifies: No referral required.

What they offer: Emergency rent and utility assistance paid directly to landlords and utilities, plus free clothing, household goods and furniture.
Who qualifies: Mecklenburg County residents for 60 days or more. Rent help may require an eviction filing, confirm current rules.
Volunteer tips: Call first. The application process starts in person.

What they offer: Access point for shelter and housing help for people who are homeless or about to lose housing.
Who qualifies: Homeless or at imminent risk in Mecklenburg County.

What they offer: 24/7 crisis support for domestic violence and sexual assault, emergency shelter and counseling.
Who qualifies: Anyone affected.
